# BAD-002 — iOS App Store rejection (2026-09-14): guest mode with optional sign-in, ads and in-app purchases unlinked, and the reply to App Review

## Brief
App Review rejected Bad Takes iOS 1.0 (build 13003, submission af7a491a-ca33-47bb-aeb6-44c6fc065230, reviewed 2026-09-14 on an iPad Air 11-inch M3, iPadOS 27.0) for three reasons:

1. Guideline 5.1.1(v): the app requires sign-in before accessing scenes. Apps may require registration only for account-based features.
2. Guideline 2.1: the binary uses AppTrackingTransparency, and the reviewer could not find the ATT prompt. Either show it with a device screen recording, or stop tracking and update App Privacy to declare no tracking.
3. Guideline 2.1(b): the app may give access to paid digital content. Apple asks who uses it, where it is bought, what previously purchased content is reachable in the app, and what is unlocked without in-app purchase.

Eric's decisions (2026-09-14):
- Guest mode with optional sign-in, on iOS and in the browser alike (the desktop keeps its gate). A signed-out user can do everything that runs on the device: add a scene from a local file, table read, record takes in the booth, play the screening, and export or share. Sign-in gates what uses Bad Takes' backend: downloading or installing scenes from the hosted catalog, and collab. Eric set the scope after Spud raised that a guest limited to watching would still have the core feature behind sign-in.
- A new guest's empty library (Kennebec's finding) is fixed by marking one or two catalog entries in the index as open to guests (remedy B). Eric picks which. The review notes also point at a sample .take file.
- For the review window, the hosted catalog is trimmed to scenes Eric can defend under 5.2.1. The index is shared, so browser users lose the unpublished scenes until they are republished.
- The public collab list is hidden on iOS, so rooms are joined by code only. Report and block are not built for this submission.
- Ads and in-app purchases are out of the iOS build for the first approval: the AdMob and RevenueCat plugins are unlinked, and the ATT usage string, the AdMob app id and SKAdNetworkItems are gone from Info.plist. The web-side ads and billing code stays dormant for later. Every mention of a paid plan disappears from the iOS app. The desktop's paid licence stays, but it unlocks nothing on iOS.
- Folded in from proposals 45 and 46: a privacy-policy and contact link in Settings, badtakes.io/privacy's iOS paragraph reworded (no ads, no tracking, no subscriptions), and BT_ADMOB_TESTING dropped from .github/workflows/mobile.yml.

Deliverables: one BadTakes PR carrying the code, the updated docs/MOBILE-STORES.md, and the design note docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-ios-app-review-guest-mode-design.md, whose § 5 holds the reply to App Review and the review notes for Eric to paste. Eric's own actions: App Store Connect (App Privacy with no tracking, detaching the subscriptions, age-rating answers, the reply); trimming the catalog and marking the guest scenes; restarting the local Supabase stack; a 0.13.4 release for the new build number.

## Size, persona and model decision
Three members, one PR. A researcher (fable, expensive if wrong: a wrong guideline read costs another review cycle) checks Eric's proposed guest scope against the App Review Guidelines and drafts the reply, in parallel with an engineer (opus) who unlinks AdMob and RevenueCat from the iOS shell and hides every plan, ad and subscription surface on iOS. A second engineer (opus) builds guest mode once the research settles the scope and the first engineer's web/ edits have returned, so their paths never overlap.

## Outcome
Landed as https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/330, squash-merged on green CI (test, test-windows, Gate and the preview deploys). Guests now use everything on the device in the web tree and on iOS; sign-in gates only unmarked Catalog downloads and Collab, and the index carries a per-entry anonymous mark. AdMob and RevenueCat are unlinked from iOS, where no plan surface shows and the public collab list is hidden. Settings has privacy and contact links, and privacy.html, mobile.yml and MOBILE-STORES.md are updated. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-ios-app-review-guest-mode-design.md holds the guideline research, the reply to App Review and the review notes. Left for Eric: mark one or two catalog scenes anonymous and trim the rest for review, the App Store Connect changes (App Privacy with no tracking, age rating, detaching the subscriptions), a 0.13.4 release, and resubmitting.
